import pytest
from target import url_basename

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url,expected",
    [
        # Empty input
        ("", ""),
        # No scheme, just domain with no path
        ("//example.com", ""),
        # Domain with trailing slash only
        ("http://example.com/", ""),
        # Single path segment
        ("http://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/bar/", "bar"),
        ("//example.com/baz", "baz"),
        # Path with query
        ("http://example.com/foo?x=1", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/a/b?x=1", "b"),
        # Path with fragment
        ("http://example.com/foo#section", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/a/b#section", "b"),
        # Multiple path segments – old regex captures the last segment
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c", "c"),
        ("https://example.com/one/two/three/four", "four"),
        # Mixed query/fragment after last segment
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c?x=1#frag", "c"),
        ("https://example.com/x/y/z#frag", "z"),
        # Path segment containing characters that are not allowed in capture
        ("http://example.com/a/b?c/d", "b"),
        # Path segment with encoded characters
        ("http://example.com/a%20b/c%20d", "c%20d"),
        # URL without leading double slash (should fail to match)
        ("example.com/foo", ""),
        # URL with extra slashes
        ("http://example.com//double//slash/", ""),
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_expected_behavior(url, expected):
    assert url_basename(url) == expected
